raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Problem

On a B300, the warp-per-row LayerNorm / RMSNorm forward took about 90-250 µs of host time per call before any GPU work, depending on host load. The kernel is 2-45 µs at the shapes below. Two costs dominate a warm call:

- `dyn()` wraps each of the six operands with `from_dlpack(...).mark_layout_dynamic()` on every call. Under cProfile, `dyn()` was the largest single cost of a warm norm call (43% of a backward call).
- `cur_stream()` reads the stream through `torch.cuda.current_stream()`, which builds a torch `Stream` object (about 6 µs).

In eager use the forward is therefore host-bound at every shape measured.

## Change

- Both warp launches, persistent and pipelined, compile once with `--enable-tvm-ffi`, on fake operands whose row count is one `cute.sym_int` (the AGENTS.md "runtime extents compile DYNAMIC" rule). Each call passes the torch tensors directly, detached when they are on an autograd tape, as `dyn()` did. The compile key is unchanged and still free of the row count.
- `cur_stream()` reads the raw handle through the existing `cudnn._torch_stream._raw_current_stream`, falling back to `torch.cuda.current_stream()`. This also helps every other norm launch that calls it.
- New helpers in `norm/utils.py`: `ffi()` and `fake_rows()`.

The kernels are untouched. The other norm routes keep `dyn()`. The backward has a pending change in its file (#2139) and can follow the same pattern once that lands.

## Measurements (B300, cc 10.3)

Following the AGENTS.md host-overhead recipe, I measured warm enqueue and captured replay separately. Develop and this branch ran in separate processes, alternating, three times.

- **`cudnn.norm.norm_fprop`, warm enqueue.** 16 cases: LayerNorm / RMSNorm, bf16 / fp16, 333-8192 rows x 1024-8192 columns, gamma passed as a `requires_grad` parameter. The median per rep was 208 / 223 / 225 µs on develop and 56 / 60 / 60 µs on this branch. The host was shared, so the absolute numbers moved between sessions: an earlier session measured 88 against 22 µs.
- **Graph API with the FROST plan selected:** warm enqueue of `g.execute`, and per-execute GPU time of a captured CUDA graph of 20 executes (medians of three reps):

| norm | rows x C | develop enqueue µs | this branch enqueue µs | develop replay µs | this branch replay µs | replay ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LayerNorm | 1024 x 1024 | 228 | 107 | 3.21 | 3.19 | 0.994 |
| LayerNorm | 4096 x 4096 | 231 | 111 | 10.82 | 10.78 | 0.996 |
| LayerNorm | 16384 x 4096 | 232 | 110 | 44.16 | 44.24 | 1.002 |
| LayerNorm | 2048 x 8192 | 230 | 110 | 11.75 | 11.77 | 1.002 |
| RMSNorm | 1024 x 1024 | 223 | 100 | 2.94 | 2.93 | 0.997 |
| RMSNorm | 4096 x 4096 | 226 | 105 | 7.75 | 7.76 | 1.001 |
| RMSNorm | 16384 x 4096 | 224 | 104 | 45.09 | 45.12 | 1.001 |
| RMSNorm | 2048 x 8192 | 226 | 105 | 8.82 | 8.78 | 0.995 |

The graph path keeps its own binding cost (`resolve_variant_pack`, `on_stream`), so it gains about 2x rather than 4x. Replay time is unchanged, within ±0.6%.

## Correctness

- **Bitwise identical to develop.** 216 output tensors (y, mean, rstd) across both entry points and all three reps match exactly.
- **CUDA graph capture.** Replay output equals eager output in every graph case.
- **New `test/python/norm/cutedsl/test_frost_norm_fwd_ffi_launch.py`:**
  - one artifact serves 1 / 300 / 4097 / 20000 rows on both warp launches, with no recompile;
  - `nn.Parameter` gamma / beta and a `requires_grad` input give results bitwise equal to the detached call;
  - a launch issued under a side stream lands on that stream, checked by a default-stream snapshot taken while the side stream is held.
- **Full `test/python/norm` on B300:** 1333 passed, 1 skipped. Develop gave 1329 passed, 1 skipped; the four extra passes are the new tests.

@@ -611,17 +611,31 @@ def forward(spec, x2d, gamma, beta, *, eps, wcfg, params, out_y=None, out_mean=N

@@ -29,6 +29,22 @@ def dyn(t):
     return from_dlpack(t, assumed_align=16).mark_layout_dynamic()
 
 
+def ffi(t):
+    """A torch tensor as a tvm-ffi launch argument: the tensor itself, detached when it is on an autograd tape (the same
+    export rule as :func:`dyn`). The tvm-ffi entry binds torch tensors natively, without a per-call DLPack round trip."""
+    return t.detach() if t.requires_grad else t
+
+
+def fake_rows(dtype, *cols, rows=None, align=16):
+    """A compile-time placeholder for a row-major ``[rows, *cols]`` operand whose row count is DYNAMIC (one compiled
+    artifact serves every R); ``rows`` is the shared ``cute.sym_int`` (pass the same symbol to every row-indexed
+    operand), ``dtype`` a cutlass element type. ``cols=()`` is a ``[rows]`` vector."""
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+
+    shape = (rows,) + tuple(cols)
+    return cute.runtime.make_fake_compact_tensor(dtype, shape, stride_order=tuple(range(len(shape) - 1, -1, -1)), assumed_align=align)
+

+

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""The warp-per-row LN / RMS forward launches through a tvm-ffi entry compiled once on a dynamic row count: torch
+tensors bind directly (no per-call DLPack export), so the compile key must stay row-count free, autograd-tape operands
+must still be accepted, and a launch must land on torch's current stream.
+
+    pytest test/python/norm/cutedsl/test_frost_norm_fwd_ffi_launch.py
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+pytest.importorskip("cudnn.norm", reason="frost norm kernels require a built cudnn frontend")
+
+from cudnn.norm._lazy import dsl_unavailable  # noqa: E402
+
+requirement_error = dsl_unavailable("FROST norm tests")
+if requirement_error:
+    pytest.skip(requirement_error, allow_module_level=True)
+
+from cudnn.norm import NormVariant, norm_fprop  # noqa: E402
+from cudnn.norm.fprop.kernels import layernorm_warp_sm100  # noqa: E402
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _sm100_family():
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() not in ((10, 0), (10, 3)):
+        pytest.skip("the SM100 norm kernels need compute capability 10.0 or 10.3")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cols", [768, 5120])  # the persistent and the pipelined warp launch
+def test_one_artifact_serves_every_row_count(cols):
+    gamma = torch.randn(cols, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    norm_fprop(NormVariant.RMS_NORM, torch.randn(7, cols, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16), gamma, None, eps=1e-6, normalized_shape=[cols])
+    compiled = len(layernorm_warp_sm100._KCACHE)
+    for rows in (1, 300, 4097, 20000):
+        x = torch.randn(rows, cols, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        y = norm_fprop(NormVariant.RMS_NORM, x, gamma, None, eps=1e-6, normalized_shape=[cols])[0]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(y.float(), F.rms_norm(x.float(), [cols], gamma.float(), eps=1e-6), atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+    assert len(layernorm_warp_sm100._KCACHE) == compiled, "a new row count recompiled the forward"
+
+
+def test_autograd_tape_operands_are_accepted():
+    x = torch.randn(512, 1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    gamma = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+    beta = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+    got = norm_fprop(NormVariant.LAYER_NORM, x.requires_grad_(), gamma, beta, eps=1e-5, normalized_shape=[1024])
+    want = norm_fprop(NormVariant.LAYER_NORM, x.detach(), gamma.detach(), beta.detach(), eps=1e-5, normalized_shape=[1024])
+    for a, b in zip(got, want):
+        assert torch.equal(a, b)
+
+
+def test_launch_lands_on_the_current_stream():
+    x = torch.randn(8192, 4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    gamma = torch.randn(4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    ref = norm_fprop(NormVariant.RMS_NORM, x, gamma, None, eps=1e-6, normalized_shape=[4096])[0]
+    out = torch.zeros_like(x)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+        torch.cuda._sleep(200_000_000)  # holds the side stream well past the snapshot below
+        norm_fprop(NormVariant.RMS_NORM, x, gamma, None, eps=1e-6, normalized_shape=[4096], out=(out, None, None))
+    snapshot = out.clone()  # on the default stream, which nothing holds: the side-stream launch has not run yet
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert not snapshot.any(), "the forward ran on a stream other than the caller's current one"
+    assert torch.equal(out, ref)

Validation: On local SM100, seven focused tests and nine graph tests passed, including all four new tests, stream ordering, changed-input replay, allocation checks and UID-zero roundtrips. An independent base/head comparison covered 36 LayerNorm/RMSNorm cases across BF16, FP16 and FP32, widths 768/5120 and row counts 1/65/4097. Outputs and statistics matched bitwise, passed an FP64 reference, remained repeatable after output poisoning, and matched after changed-input graph replay. Changing row counts did not recompile. The raw-stream fallback also passed on default and side streams. Four alternating BF16 spot checks reduced median warm direct-call host time from 104–135 microseconds to 25–37 microseconds. Captured GPU time stayed within about 0.4% of the base. These measurements used a shared SM100 GPU. Requested python/norm CI for this head, covering the new CuTe DSL tests and the graph/torch norm suites. Style passed; Security is running. The CI integration matches all three changed files.

Limitations: Remote CI remains pending. No independent SM103 measurement, graph API host-time comparison, sanitizer run or cross-device repeatability claim.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
